claim: The first nine-darter ever on TV paid 8X more than winning the whole tournament.
answer:
John Lowe hit it on 13 Oct 1984 at the MFI World Matchplay against Keith Deller. The bonus: £102,000. For lifting the trophy he got just £12,000.

Bonus fact: viewers didn't even see it live. ITV showed it later in the highlights.
sources: Dr Patrick Chaplin (darts historian), MasterCaller prize-money archive, Wikipedia

claim: The numbers on the dartboard were arranged by a carpenter called Brian Gamlin in 1896.
answer:
Almost every darts book repeats it. But darts historian Dr Patrick Chaplin hunted for Gamlin for years and found no record he ever existed.

His best lead: a Yorkshire wire-worker named Thomas Buckle, around 1912.

claim: Phil Taylor once hit two nine-darters in the same match.
answer:
24 May 2010, Premier League final against James Wade at Wembley. A perfect leg in leg 2, another one in leg 15, and he won 10–8.

Wade later said that without those two nine-darters, Taylor would not have won.

claim: Darts was saved in 1908 when a player hit three 20s in front of a judge.
answer:
The story: Leeds landlord Jim Garside was charged with allowing a 'game of chance'. His best player, 'Bigfoot' Annakin, threw in court and the case was dismissed.

The catch: single, double or treble 20? Every version differs. No newspaper reported it and the court records are gone.

claim: Phil Taylor threw the first nine-darter ever shown live on TV.
answer:
That was Shaun Greatbatch, the 'Nine Dart Man': 3 Feb 2002, Dutch Open final against Steve Coote, live on Dutch TV.

Taylor followed six months later with the first live one on British TV, at the 2002 World Matchplay.
sources: Dr Patrick Chaplin (darts historian), DartsNews, Wikipedia

claim: Before his first World Championship, Luke Littler had fewer than 5,000 Instagram followers.
answer:
He had about 4,000. Within weeks he became the first darts player ever to pass 1 million. Today it's more than 1.9 million.

He admitted he stayed up until 5 am refreshing the app to watch the number climb.
sources: Associated Press, The Irish Times, Front Office Sports

claim: The 'oche' got its name from a brewery called Hockey & Sons.
answer:
Plenty of darts sites still claim it. Darts historian Dr Patrick Chaplin says it's flat-out untrue.

The oldest written uses from the 1930s spell it 'hockey'. 'Oche' only became standard in the late 1970s, and the real origin is still unknown.
sources: Dr Patrick Chaplin (darts historian), World Wide Words (Michael Quinion)
